source: onsemi press release: onsemi Introduces the Embedded Power Platform, a (09-16-2026)

quarterly_data.signal: onsemi unveiled the Embedded Power Platform (EPP), which uses the silicon wafer itself as the package and embeds multiple devices (FETs, drivers, controllers) integrating silicon, SiC and GaN in a wafer-level architecture, built on onsemi's standard 12-inch silicon wafer manufacturing. The company says EPP enables up to 3 - 5x higher power density depending on the application and development cycles as little as four months. For AI infrastructure, an early EPP-based solid-state circuit-breaker design was approximately 50% smaller and 20% cooler than existing designs; for EV traction inverters it cites up to 4x higher power density and 15% lower power losses versus conventional approaches. Subaru Corporation is one of the first early engagement partners, evaluating EPP for future electrified vehicle architectures with early access to engineering samples. Availability: 'EPP is expected to begin sampling in 2026 with strategic customers and ecosystem participants across automotive and AI applications.'
quarterly_data.figure: 3 - 5x higher power density; 12-inch wafers; circuit breaker approximately 50% smaller and 20% cooler; sampling expected in 2026
